flags.text: The investor gets 2x their money back before anyone else shares in a sale. 1x is the usual ask at this stage.
flags.title: Liquidation preference above 1x
flags.ai_text: In plain words: The investor gets 2x their money back before anyone else shares in a sale. 1x is the usual ask at this stage.

flags.text: The investor takes their money back first and then also shares in what is left (double dip), up to 3x in total.
flags.title: Participating preferred
flags.ai_text: In plain words: The investor takes their money back first and then also shares in what is left (double dip), up to 3x in total.

flags.text: The option pool is 18% of the pre-money. Because it sits in the pre-money, founders carry all of that dilution.
flags.title: Large option pool in the pre-money
flags.ai_text: In plain words: The option pool is 18% of the pre-money. Because it sits in the pre-money, founders carry all of that dilution.

flags.text: You agree not to talk to other investors for 60 days. Up to 45 days is common.
flags.title: Long exclusivity (no-shop)
flags.ai_text: In plain words: You agree not to talk to other investors for 60 days. Up to 45 days is common.

flags.text: The investor gets 2 board seats on a seed round. At this stage one seat, or an observer, is more common.
flags.title: More than one investor board seat on an early round

flags.text: The investor can buy more than their share of future rounds, which can crowd out new investors.
flags.title: Super pro-rata
flags.ai_text: In plain words: The investor can buy more than their share of future rounds, which can crowd out new investors.

flags.text: If you later raise at a lower price, the investor's price resets all the way down to it. Broad-based weighted average is the usual protection.
